intro-0.text: Detective Dima? Iris Vasilescu. Thirty-four. Found dead yesterday morning. A head injury the first report cannot explain. The room is yours.
intro-0.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

intro-1.text: Her sister called twice while we waited. First she asked what had happened. Then she asked if the lamp was still on.
intro-1.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

intro-2.text: Leave it on. I will start with the room.
intro-2.speaker: Alex Dima

intro-3.text: Nothing has been put back. There is an authorised phone copy on the side table. Take your time. Then tell me what you can actually establish.
intro-3.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

question-object.text: What should the search team be looking for?
question-object.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

question-source.text: Which original gives us the latest known view of it still here?
question-source.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

question-layout.text: Then what do you make of the furniture?
question-layout.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

question-limit.text: And what can that comparison establish? Be precise.
question-limit.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

welcome.text: Iris was found here yesterday. The body is with the examiner. I have kept the room as it was. Start with the room and the phone copy. I will wait on the landing.
welcome.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

family.text: Elena. Her sister. She asked me to leave the lamp on. I do not think she meant it as evidence.
family.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

room.text: The photographs were taken before removal. We have not straightened a chair or returned anything to a shelf. That is all I can tell you about the arrangement.
room.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

hypothesis.text: All right. Show me the difference, and something that tells us when it was already there. A room can change for more than one reason.
hypothesis.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

notYet.text: You have a possibility. I need a comparison. Keep the original image, not just the impression it gives you.
notYet.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

wrong.text: That does not agree with the originals you have shown me. Keep looking. We do not need an answer quickly; we need one that holds.
wrong.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

bounded.text: There is an interval. Do not turn it into a time of death, or a name. What can the two sources actually establish?
bounded.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

finding.text: Yes. The earlier original changes the question. I will have the search request written that way. You have kept what the image can prove separate from what it cannot.
finding.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

next.text: The receiving desk at the Aurelia has kept its own records. I will arrange access. Leave this room as it is; we may need to come back to it.
next.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

hint1.text: Do not start with a person. Start with what is physically different between this room and an original photograph.
hint1.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

hint2.text: A photograph can belong to a different day. Check the original capture information before using a changed arrangement to explain the death.
hint2.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

hint3.text: There is a retained image inside the unsent message. Compare both the furniture and the lower shelf. You can zoom, and use the image description if that is clearer.
hint3.speaker: Sergeant Petrescu

iris.text: Do not throw the blue mug out. It only leaks if I put anything in it. And please do not fix it so well that it stops being my mug.
iris.speaker: Iris
